subject: RapidRetail: p95/p99 latency regression & token/s throughput drop
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@rapidretail.com>
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production impact: p95/p99 and dramatic tokens/sec drop

Hi Priya,

We're seeing a production regression that started late yesterday evening (UTC). p95 and p99 latencies for our primary inference route spiked ~3x and token-per-second throughput collapsed from ~1.5k tps to ~250-350 tps for the same request profile. Error-rate is slightly up (mostly 500s) when the downstream queue backs up.

This is customer-facing and impacting the checkout recommendation flow. We rolled no changes client-side. I attached a small packet of logs and a heap of request IDs.

Key observations from our side:
- Spike began ~2027-05-09T01:40:00Z
- Affected model: rr-reco-v2 (served via hosted-inference east-1)
- Sequences typically ~800-1200 tokens (long tail)
- CPU and network on our end look normal

Can you confirm whether anything was changed on your side (quantization profile, runtime/kernels, deployment)? We need an ETA and mitigation plan — this is in PROD.

Thanks — Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of ML Engineering, RapidRetail
attachments: rapid_logs_20270509.zip (logs)

From: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@rapidretail.com>
Cc: support@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-09T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact: p95/p99 and dramatic tokens/sec drop

Thanks for the heads-up, Samantha — I'm sorry you're seeing this. I'm opening an incident and looping in SRE and our inference engineering leads.

Immediate next steps:
- Incident created: JIRA-INC-4821 (we'll attach telemetry to the ticket)
- Can you confirm the request IDs you pasted are the ones in rapid_logs_20270509.zip?
- We're going to pull kernel/runtime change logs for the last 24h and check for quantization profile rollouts and kernel selector changes.

Short term mitigation we're considering (will confirm in 30–45 minutes):
- Force model to use the pre-quantized execution path (disable automatic kernel switching) for rr-reco-v2 in east-1
- If that restores tps, we will schedule a targeted rollback of last night's runtime config for that pool and run a two-hour canary.

CCing: rishi.malhotra, markus.klein, monica.patel, logan.wright for escalation/credit decisions.

I'll follow up shortly with telemetry snapshot.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
attachments: none

From: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: logan.wright@redwood.ai, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@rapidretail.com>, support@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-09T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: URGENT: RapidRetail production regression — suspected kernel/quantization path change

Team — RapidRetail's p95/p99 and tokens/sec dropped dramatically in hosted east-1. Timeline aligns with a runtime change deployed 2027-05-09 00:30 UTC: automatic kernel selector was updated to prefer new int8-v2 kernels for certain transformer blocks and we also rolled a new quantization profile for rr-reco-v2.

Preliminary telemetry (attached): perf-graphs.png, kernel-selection-diff.txt, profiler-snippet.txt show:
- p95/p99 increase concentrated on sequences >1024 tokens
- overall tokens/sec dropped ~75% for affected requests
- Kernel switch events rose at 00:31 UTC for the host pool serving rr-reco-v2
- Memory bandwidth and L2 utilization spikes correlate with the new int8-v2 kernel path

Requesting immediate actions:
1) Can one of you push an emergency config to force fp16-kernel fallback for rr-reco-v2 in east-1 and disable the int8-v2 selector? (This should be a routing config change, not a model reupload.)
2) If (1) is effective, we'll run a 2-hour canary and then revert the runtime selector change for that pool and investigate kernel perf regressions offline.
3) If rollback fails to restore performance, prepare a hotfix to the kernel (Rishi) and an emergency quantization rollback (Monica).

Customer is requesting ETA and whether we'll provide SLA credits. Logan, can you advise on credit guidance if we need an SLA remediation?

Attachments: kernel-selection-diff.txt; perf-graphs.png; profiler-snippet.txt

— Priya

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: logan.wright@redwood.ai, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@rapidretail.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: RapidRetail production regression — suspected kernel/quantization path change

Confirming I've pulled the profiler traces. Quick findings:
- The int8-v2 path adds an extra gather+remap microkernel for KV cache layout before attention, which increases memory traffic for long sequences. On our A100 host config that results in L2 thrash + lower per-GPU token emission for long sequences.
- The quantization tweak we rolled reduced activation clipping for some layers which appears to increase internal dynamic range and forces the int8-v2 path to run more branches.

Immediate mitigation implemented (11:30 UTC):
- Pushed config to force fp16 execution for model tag rr-reco-v2 in pool-east-1 (non-disruptive config change).
- Disabled automatic kernel selector for the pool (will revert after canary).

Preliminary results: tokens/sec for sampled trace climbed from ~320 -> ~1,420 within 12 minutes; p95 dropped back near baseline. Error rate dropped as queue drained.

Next steps:
- Monitor for 2 hours, run regression tests on int8-v2 microkernels for long sequences offline.
- If stable, we will revert the last night's selector change for the pool and quarantine the int8-v2 rollout.
- Prepare a changelog and postmortem for RapidRetail; include perf counter evidence and recommendations for safe rollout thresholds (seq length, memory headroom).

Rishi
Principal Inference Engineer — Redwood Inference
attachments: profiler-snippet.txt

From: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@rapidretail.com>, Alex Cho <alex.cho@rapidretail.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, logan.wright@redwood.ai, support@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-09T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact: p95/p99 and dramatic tokens/sec drop — update & next steps

Samantha / Alex — quick update and proposal:

Summary: we rolled an emergency config at 11:30 UTC to force fp16 kernels for rr-reco-v2 and disable the new kernel selector. That change restored tokens/sec to within ~95% of baseline for sampled traffic and reduced p95/p99. The queue drained and error-rate returned to normal.

Planned next steps (we want your sign-off):
1) Run a 2-hour canary on the pool starting as soon as you confirm any live traffic window constraints (we suggest 12:30–14:30 UTC).
2) If canary remains stable, we will roll a targeted rollback of the kernel selector change for pool-east-1 and block the int8-v2 rollout until we finish kernel perf validation.
3) Postmortem & timeline: we will deliver a root-cause analysis and remediation plan within 3 business days.

Credits: Logan, our GTM lead, is on the thread to coordinate SLA remediation. Logan — if we confirm a >1 hour partial outage from 01:40–02:55 UTC and residual degradation, what's the typical credit band we should offer RapidRetail?

Samantha — appreciate the quick signal and the logs. If you can confirm the request IDs you sent map to the traces in rapid_logs_20270509.zip, we will attach that to the postmortem.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
